arguments.premise_synthesis: When short-term rates are lowered to accommodate political pressure, the government borrows and spends more, increasing the money supply. This monetary expansion leads to rising prices, and rational lenders demand higher long-term rates to compensate for anticipated inflation. Recent observations show long-term Treasury yields rising despite short-term cuts, consistent with this mechanism.
arguments.conclusion_supported: The prediction that lowering short-term rates under political influence will cause long-term rates to rise, contradicting the typical yield curve flattening expectation, due to inflation fears from monetary expansion.
